title: Ukraine Can Turn Imminent Peril to Its Advantage
gist: Eric Ciaramella says Ukraine faces its most precarious moment since the early war as Russia intensifies long-range strikes with ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, and is reportedly planning a harsher winter campaign against energy and water. The title proposes a true 'energy cease-fire' as leverage; only the opening is available (paywall).

insights.claim: Since late July, Russia has used a growing stockpile of ballistic missiles and a new generation of jet-powered drones to dramatically intensify long-range attacks on Ukrainian population centers, focusing on logistics, transportation and commercial infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Eric Ciaramella
insights.so_what: Rising strike intensity raises risk to Ukrainian logistics, commercial assets and grain and transport corridors.

insights.claim: According to Ukrainian intelligence reports, Russia is planning an even more intense campaign against Ukrainian energy and water supplies this winter in an attempt to decisively break Ukraine's economy and society.
insights.speaker: Eric Ciaramella
insights.so_what: Winter strikes on power and water raise European gas and power-market and refugee-flow risk; monitor Ukrainian grid outages.

insights.claim: The author argues a true 'energy cease-fire' could curb Putin and let Ukraine turn its peril into an advantage.
insights.speaker: Eric Ciaramella
insights.so_what: A mutual halt on energy-infrastructure strikes would be a trackable de-escalation signal for energy markets.
insights.quote: How a True “Energy Cease-Fire” Can Curb Putin
